A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same StarDojo study, with all 36 pages and Appendices A–E available. Pages 2–36 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; differences are confined to title-page affiliation references and arXiv metadata.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of seven MLLMs on StarDojo-Lite in Table 3, error analysis and ablations in Figures 4–5, and agent trajectory case studies in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including Table 3, Figures 4–5, and Appendix E. Their retention from v3 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: The StarDojoMod architecture, observation/action interfaces, pause-and-resume mechanism, and task evaluator are identical in Sections 3.2–3.4 and Appendix B, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 100-task StarDojo-Lite suite across farming, crafting, exploration, combat, and social interaction. The task list and five-task ablation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains exactly the same seven models: GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Llama 4 Maverick, Qwen2.5 VL 72B, and Gemma 3 27B.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain 720p images, 7×7 textual surroundings, at most two actions per response, and 30/50/150-step limits for easy/medium/hard tasks. Evaluation metrics and ablation protocols are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the same GPT-4.1 error analysis and image-only, text-only, and real-time ablations. Appendix E contains identical error examples and successful/failed trajectories.

E5.justification: Table 3 reports the same success rates with standard deviations over three runs. The three-run reporting in Section 4, Figure 5's caption, and Appendix C is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical, including GPT-4.1's 12.7 ± 0.6% overall success rate in Table 3, error proportions in Figure 4, ablations in Figure 5, costs in Table 6, and Appendix E trajectories.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, or derivations are revised. Neither version contains theorem-and-proof development, and the evaluation pseudocode is identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about combining production and social activities, the 1,000-task benchmark and 100-task subset, the unified interface, and substantial limitations of current MLLM agents.

C2.justification: The explanations of navigation failures, multimodal reasoning difficulties, and inference-latency tradeoffs are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning game access, fishing, advanced maps, social scope, and evaluation coverage.

D1.justification: Implementation documentation, model identifiers, simulator APIs, installation instructions, prompts, and cost information remain identical in Section 4 and Appendices B–D. The project access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Table 1's positioning against other environments, and all 49 references are identical. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: Title-page affiliation superscripts change for Mingcong Lei from 2 to 3, Yitian Hong from 3 to 4, and Xinrun Wang from 4 to 5. The arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 28 June 2026 to v4 dated 26 August 2026. Body wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–6, their captions, and their placement are identical, including the appendices. The title page retains the same layout despite its affiliation and version-text updates.

improvement.justification: The revision updates affiliation references and arXiv metadata only. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and presentation of the body and appendices remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
